source_text: Pecunia Domini sunt eloquia Domini — argentum igne probatum. Si male doceo, pecunia mea reproba; si bene, fenus iustum. Misericordiam volo quam sacrificium.
thought_title: The Lord's money is his tested words
orientation: Origen is explaining that the words of the Lord are the Lord's money, tested silver, and that a teacher's teaching is either approved or rejected money.
pass_a_gloss: Money [of the] Lord are [the] words [of the] Lord — silver [by] fire tested. If badly I teach, money my reprobate; if well, interest just. Mercy I wish rather than sacrifice.

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of money as the tested words of God, per the glossary.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for the Lord's sayings.
Literal rendering of the ablative of means and the participle, preserving the image of testing.
Keeps the financial metaphor of teaching as lending money that yields interest.

choices.english: I want mercy rather than sacrifice
choices.why: Literal rendering of the comparative construction, preserving the biblical wording.

pass_b_english: The money of the Lord is the words of the Lord—silver tested by fire. If I teach badly, my money is rejected; if I teach well, it is a just interest. I want mercy rather than sacrifice.

problems.quote: I want mercy rather than sacrifice (Hosea 6:6)
problems.why: Source lacks any scripture citation; Hosea 6:6 is editorial addition not in Latin.
problems.fix: I want mercy rather than sacrifice.
problems.ruling: Latin source 'Misericordiam volo quam sacrificium' has no citation; '(Hosea 6:6)' is editorial addition not in source.

edits.old: I want mercy rather than sacrifice (Hosea 6:6).
edits.new: I want mercy rather than sacrifice.

fixed: Removed editorial scripture citation (Hosea 6:6) not present in the Latin source.

last_rejected.quote: I want mercy rather than sacrifice
last_rejected.why: Latin 'volo' is 1st person singular, but context shows this is God speaking through Hosea 6:6 / Matthew 9:13, not Origen's own desire. English 'I want' makes it sound like Origen's personal statement, not a divine quotation.
last_rejected.fix: 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice'—the Lord's words, not mine.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'volo' is 1st person singular, matching the biblical quotation; 'I want' correctly renders the speaker's words.

last_rejected.quote: I want mercy rather than sacrifice
last_rejected.why: The English hides that these are God's words (Scripture quotation), making them appear as Origen's own statement and obscuring the shift in speaker.
last_rejected.fix: As the Lord says, 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice'
last_rejected.ruling: Latin has no quotation marks either; 'I want' faithfully renders 'volo' without obscuring speaker more than source does.
